extracted.intended_audience: students/practitioners of arithmetic and elementary number theory (early-modern/classical context)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and methods for producing, combining, and recognizing square numbers (numeri quadrati): including adding/subtracting parts, halving/partitioning, multiplication of members of families, cross-multiplication, use of roots, Euclidean composition/decomposition, and geometric/figurative arrangement to obtain new square numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regole per ottenere numeri quadrati congrui
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to make a given number or set of numbers into 'quadrati congrui' by adding or subtracting suitable quantities (phrases: "le regole cifere cogrucri e lo: qnadrari pgrui fojmari", "tu voi giognere e trare").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly explains that to obtain a congruent square one may add or subtract particular terms; specific small numerical examples are given (e.g. references to 12, 169, 144) to show how adding or removing parts produces the intended square. The author emphasizes following stepwise rules (non‑arbitrary additions/subtractions) rather than random adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moltiplicazione di numeri per ottenere quadrati
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiplication of numbers (including multiplying elements of one set by elements of another) to produce square numbers (phrases: "multiplica vno in laltro", "moltiplica i fe fora ... farà quadrato").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and computations show multiplying members of families to form numbers whose product is a square (e.g., products reaching 400, 4·100, etc.). Guidance includes selecting which factors to multiply so resulting products become perfect squares and using repeated multiplications when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prendere la metà e altre parti per formare quadrati
rubrics_metrics.description: Forming squares by partitioning numbers into halves, quarters, or other fractional parts (phrases: "piglia la mita", "la mita ... nc caua el meno2C numero quadro").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method: take the half (or quarter) of an appropriate sum/term as an intermediate, then use that part to construct another square or to combine with other parts. Several worked numeric examples illustrate when halving yields components that lead to squares or to further multiplications producing squares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinazione di infiemi di quadrati per formare un quadrato
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine families (insiemi) of square numbers so that together they form a larger square (phrases: "infiemi ... fanno il numero quadrato", "li numeri quadrati gioti infiemi facino numero quadrato").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author advises grouping square numbers with attention to parity (even/odd), proportions, and relative positions; examples list families (e.g., sets of 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64) and show how sums/products of selected members yield another perfect square.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uso delle radici (estrarre radici) per determinare componenti quadrate
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate with square roots to determine which numbers or combinations yield squares (phrases: "radici", "la radici ... lo quale poi ... la radici ...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text uses root extraction both to check when a constructed number is a square and to reverse-engineer components (take root, see remaining factor). Guidance includes examples of testing candidates by taking square roots and verifying integer results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metodo euclideo di composizione/decomposizione
rubrics_metrics.description: Compose and decompose numbers by factorization in the Euclidean manner to identify or create square numbers (mentions Euclid: 'Euclidc' and composition of natural square numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author indicates that decomposing numbers into factors (and recomposing them) according to Euclidean ideas allows systematic generation of squares; this includes multiplying factors in matching ways so that exponents of prime factors become even, producing perfect squares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uso delle proporzioni e rapporti per trovare quadrati
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit proportions/ratios (fractions, parti proporzionali) between numbers to derive squares (phrases: "proportione", "fra ... la proportione ...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures include forming proportional parts, using cross-multiplication and scaling so that proportional relationships convert existing numbers into squares. The text gives examples where selecting proportional parts produces numbers whose products or sums are squares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moltiplicazioni incrociate (crocetta) fra famiglie
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine elements from different families via cross-multiplication ('crocetta') to produce new square numbers (phrases: "crocetta", "la fuma odi icrociamcti").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed examples show taking products across rows/columns (figurative 'cross') of selected family elements; the resulting combinations are then analyzed to see which produce perfect squares. The author explains arranging elements so cross-products align to square structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riduzione/divisione in parti uguali come procedura
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce numbers by dividing into equal parts as a step toward forming squares (phrases: "Divide in due parti equali", "prendi la mita e..." ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure often precedes multiplication or recombination: partition a given number into equal parts, manipulate those parts (e.g., multiply or add), and reassemble to obtain squares. The text gives stepwise numeric demonstrations emphasizing equal partitioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moltiplicazioni ripetute e scalature per ottenere quadrati
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply repeated multiplications (multiplying by various powers or sequences) and scaling of numbers to turn non-squares into squares (phrases: "moltiplica ... poi moltiplica pur ... multiplicariós ... ripetute").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include multiplying by squares or by factors that make all prime exponents even; instructions show sequences (e.g., multiply by 2, then by 4, then by 25, etc.) until the product is a perfect square. Guidance warns to track factors to avoid unnecessary operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposizione geometrica/figurativa per guidare operazioni
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange numbers in figures or geometrical diagrams to guide which operations will produce squares (phrases: "figure geometridx", "metti nella figura ...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author suggests laying out numbers in visual arrays (rows, crosses, 'crocetta') to see combinatorial patterns and proportional positions that make constructing squares more evident; this approach connects arithmetic manipulations with geometric intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principio metodico: operare razionalmente, non arbitrariamente
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate by rational, rule‑based steps rather than by arbitrary manipulation (phrase: "si intende razionale e no altramète").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Across the exposition the author stresses following the prescribed rules/algorithms (halving, multiplying factors, using proportions, arranging in families) and cautions against random guesses; examples illustrate failures when operations are done without the indicated method.
